analysis:
CHANGELOG.md is documentation only. The supplied units (head lines 2816-3290) show historical release notes. The patch excerpt shows the v0.10.8 candidate header and upgrade notes being added above them. There is no code, configuration, cryptographic, authorization, attestation or cache-storage change in the supplied evidence, so no control is weakened.

The historical text in these units describes controls rather than changing them. It covers the SSD write budget, the encrypted prefix cache with a coordinator-authored scope, App Attest handling, the provider logout and revocation path, and the MDM cohort freeze. These statements are consistent with the retained threat model entries T-041, T-053, T-054 and T-057. None contradicts them.

T-041 and the 30-minute TTL: the text in these units that mentions the cache does not raise the TTL above 30 minutes or weaken account isolation. It mentions the 4 TB per-day write budget, which is a write-endurance control and not a TTL or scoping change.

Limits of this review: the v0.10.8 additions are only partly visible, because the patch excerpt is truncated and incomplete. The pair-update, cluster-pairing and auto-update notes it begins to describe are outside the supplied evidence. If other batches contain code for those features, the next pass should check the following. First, same-build pairing and mutual authentication. Second, the update path integrity and verification, which falls under T-043, T-013 and T-034. Third, the 64-approval registration limit on the coordinator. This changelog gives no evidence of a regression in any of these, and those code paths remain unverified here.
